hook_hypotheses.hook_text: Could you survive one nanosecond in every layer of the Sun? The answer changes depending on which layer you enter.
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Immediate survival question and layer-dependent constraint.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: Which solar layer delivers the most damaging exposure in one nanosecond?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Compare density, radiation flux, and temperature across solar layers without promising survival.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Direct questions and immediate premises recur across both formats; solar exposure analogues are high-relative performers.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Direct-question openings also occur in weak videos; SURVIVE family cohesion is low.
risks: Survival depends on exposure geometry and layer definitions.
No retention data supports exact opening length.

hook_hypotheses.hook_text: One nanosecond is one billionth of a second. Inside the Sun, that can still mean three very different exposures.
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Scale anchor first, solar-layer comparison second.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: Can an almost vanishing exposure time still transfer dangerous energy?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Quantify what changes between sparse hot plasma and denser solar material.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Number-led and limit/measurement structures repeat among high-relative examples, especially Shorts.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Most number-led support comes from Shorts; long-form transfer is unproven.
risks: Scale statement must not substitute for a physical energy calculation.

hook_hypotheses.hook_text: The Sun's hottest layer may not be the layer that hurts you most in one nanosecond. Temperature is only one part of the exposure.
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Contradiction first, limiting variables immediately named.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: Which variable overturns the obvious temperature-only answer?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Resolve the solar hazard comparison using temperature, density, radiation, and time.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Counterpoint-led explanations and escalation structures recur, but are mixed across performance bands.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Declarative openings have weak and normal examples; no private retention comparison exists.
risks: Must avoid implying hotter is safer.

hook_hypotheses.hook_text: Could Earth ever produce a magnitude 10 earthquake? The scale allows it, but the planet may not.
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Immediate feasibility question followed by mathematical-versus-physical distinction.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: What physical limit stops an open-ended magnitude scale?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Separate scale mathematics from Earth's available fault geometry.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Earthquake questions appear in high-relative Shorts and long-form examples.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Earthquake family has only two close long-form/Shorts analogues and disaster framing is crowded.
risks: Must not imply magnitude 10 has occurred.
Scale and intensity must remain distinct.

hook_hypotheses.hook_text: Earthquake magnitude has no mathematical maximum. Earth has a finite size, so the real question is what fault the planet can supply.
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Apparent contradiction stated first, physical constraint second.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: How does finite fault size bound a mathematically open scale?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Show how fault length and rupture area constrain an Earth earthquake.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Constraint and counterpoint phases recur in channel scripts; exact earthquake items exceed channel median.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Declarative title/package evidence is weaker channel-wide and n=2 is insufficient for a repeated winner.
risks: Must avoid presenting one exact universal ceiling.

hook_hypotheses.hook_text: To make a magnitude 10 earthquake on Earth, start with the fault. How long would it need to be before the planet itself becomes the constraint?
hook_hypotheses.premise_delivery: Physical constraint and calculation target arrive before consequence framing.
hook_hypotheses.open_loop: Does Earth contain a fault large enough for the target magnitude?
hook_hypotheses.expected_payoff: Estimate required rupture scale, then compare it with Earth's fault geometry.
hook_hypotheses.historical_support: Calculation and constraint phases repeat in explanatory scripts; limit/measurement titles have positive public-performance association.
hook_hypotheses.counter_evidence: Fault length alone does not determine every earthquake effect; historical package-performance alignment is unknown.
risks: Do not conflate magnitude with local shaking intensity.

script_blueprints.opening: State one-nanosecond solar exposure and identify layer choice as the controlling comparison.
script_blueprints.core_premise: Exposure outcome depends on energy transfer, density, radiation, and time rather than temperature alone.
constraints: Hold exposure time and body geometry constant.
Separate heat, radiation, and particle interactions.
script_blueprints.escalation: Move from sparse outer plasma to denser regions while keeping one-nanosecond duration fixed.
intermediate_payoffs: Why hottest does not automatically mean most damaging.
Which exposure channel dominates in each region.
script_blueprints.main_payoff: A bounded solar-layer hazard comparison showing which assumptions control one-nanosecond exposure.
script_blueprints.counterpoint: No single result applies to every depth, geometry, or harm definition.
script_blueprints.ending: Restate conditional answer and unresolved assumptions without survival certainty.
script_blueprints.historical_support: Calculation-plus-escalation structures and solar exposure analogues recur in canonical transcripts.
risks: Public views do not prove structure caused performance.
script_blueprints.what_not_to_overclaim: Do not claim guaranteed survival, an exact injury threshold, or a proven retention structure.

script_blueprints.opening: Separate open-ended magnitude mathematics from finite Earth physics.
script_blueprints.core_premise: Earthquake magnitude has no mathematical hard maximum, while Earth's rupture geometry imposes practical limits.
constraints: Separate recorded events from hypothetical calculations.
script_blueprints.escalation: Increase target magnitude and show rapidly growing rupture requirements.
intermediate_payoffs: Why terrestrial fault dimensions do not.
script_blueprints.main_payoff: A conditional Earth earthquake limit based on rupture geometry, without inventing one universal maximum.
script_blueprints.counterpoint: Magnitude alone does not describe local damage, and fault length is not the only physical variable.
script_blueprints.ending: Return to the scale-versus-planet distinction and state the bounded conclusion.
script_blueprints.historical_support: Earthquake analogues span Shorts and long-form; calculation, constraint, and qualification phases recur.
risks: Disaster framing can outrun the evidence.
script_blueprints.what_not_to_overclaim: Do not claim magnitude 10 has occurred, fault length alone predicts effects, or structure is a retention winner.
